title: Calculus I
description: Limits, derivatives and integrals of one-variable functions, including transcendental functions, with applications and a lab component.
prereq_text: MATH 198 or 199 or equivalent, or a qualifying high school pre-calculus/calculus grade.
notes: Entry is by math placement, so the planner treats it as having no prerequisites.

title: Calculus II
description: Integration techniques, polar coordinates, vectors, improper integrals, and sequences and series.
prereq_text: MATH 226 with a C or better.

title: Introduction to Linear Algebra
description: Solving linear systems, matrix algebra, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and orthogonality, using MATLAB for computation.
prereq_text: MATH 198, 199 or 226 with a C or better.

title: Probability and Statistics with Computing
description: Probability, random variables and distributions, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing, with data analysis in statistical software.
prereq_text: MATH 227 with a C or better; computer experience approved by the instructor.
notes: Instructor approval of computer experience is not encoded.

title: General Physics with Calculus I
description: Calculus-based classical mechanics: motion, forces, energy, momentum, rotation, oscillations and gravitation.
prereq_text: MATH 226 with a C or better; concurrent enrollment in PHYS 222.

title: General Physics with Calculus I Laboratory
description: Laboratory experiments in mechanics that accompany PHYS 220.
prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in PHYS 220.

title: General Physics with Calculus II
description: Calculus-based electricity and magnetism: circuits, magnetic fields, induction, electromagnetic waves and Maxwell's equations.
prereq_text: PHYS 220 and MATH 227 with a C or better; concurrent enrollment in PHYS 232.

title: General Physics with Calculus II Laboratory
description: Laboratory experiments in electricity and magnetism that accompany PHYS 230.
prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in PHYS 230.

title: Introduction to Computing
description: First programming course for students with no background: problem solving, basic programming in Java, and the role of computing in society.
prereq_text: None.

title: Intermediate Computer Programming
description: Designing, testing and debugging Java programs, object-oriented programming, and basic software development tools.
prereq_text: CSC 101 with a C or better.

title: Data Structures
description: Linear and non-linear data structures in Java (lists, stacks, queues, trees, hash tables, graphs), recursion, sorting, searching and Big-O analysis.
prereq_text: CSC 210 or CSC 215 with a C or better.
notes: CSC 210 is an older/transfer equivalent and is not in this dataset; it counts only if listed as completed.

title: Discrete Mathematical Structures for Computer Science
description: Sets, relations, functions, logic, proof techniques, counting and graph theory as used in computer science.
prereq_text: CSC 210 or 215 or ENGR 213, and MATH 227 (may be taken concurrently), with a C or better.
notes: MATH 227 may be taken in the same semester, so it is a coreq (same semester or earlier), not a prereq.

title: Machine Structures
description: Digital logic, data representation, assembly language programming, CPU organization and memory systems.
prereq_text: CSC 230 with a C or better.

title: Ethics, Communication, and Tools for Software Development (GWAR)
description: Professional ethics, privacy, security and legal issues in software, technical writing and communication, and team collaboration tools such as version control.
prereq_text: Upper-division CS majors/minors; GE Area A2; CSC 210 or CSC 215.
notes: Upper-division standing and GE Area A2 are not encoded.

title: Introduction to Web Software Development
description: UNIX basics and web development: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, client- and server-side programming, and connecting web apps to databases.
prereq_text: CSC 220 or permission of the instructor.
notes: Permission-of-instructor path is out of scope.

title: Programming Methodology
description: Advanced data structures and algorithms in C++: design and implementation, sorting, searching and graph algorithms.
prereq_text: CSC 220 and CSC 230 with a C or better.

title: Software Development
description: Object-oriented design and the software lifecycle: requirements, design, testing, user interfaces and maintenance on larger projects.
prereq_text: CSC 220 and CSC 317 with a C or better.

title: Operating System Principles
description: Processes, threads, concurrency and synchronization, deadlock, scheduling, memory management, file systems and security, with systems programming in C.
prereq_text: CSC 256, CSC 340, MATH 324 and PHYS 230 with a C or better, or graduate standing.

title: Analysis of Algorithms I
description: Algorithm design techniques (divide and conquer, greedy, dynamic programming) and time/space complexity analysis applied to classic problems.
prereq_text: CSC 340 and MATH 324 with a C or better.

title: Software Engineering
description: Capstone team project applying software engineering methods, tools and agile teamwork to build a full application.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; CSC 317 and CSC 413 with a C or better; GPA 3.0 or instructor permission.
notes: GPA and permission conditions are not encoded. CSC 648 is the major capstone.

title: Theory of Computing
description: Automata, regular and context-free languages, Turing machines, computability and undecidable problems.
prereq_text: CSC 220 and CSC 230; MATH 225 or MATH 325; C or better.

title: Natural Language Technologies
description: Natural language processing concepts and algorithms, text processing, and building real-world language applications.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; CSC 413 with a C or better; GPA 3.0 or instructor permission.

title: Human-Computer Interaction
description: User-centered design, prototyping, implementation and usability evaluation of user interfaces.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; CSC 413 with a C or better, or instructor permission.

title: Computer Networks
description: Network architecture and protocols, the TCP/IP stack, network design, testing and standards.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; CSC 415 with a C or better; GPA 3.0 or instructor permission.

title: Introduction to Security and Data Privacy
description: Cybersecurity fundamentals, cryptography, threats and defenses, and data privacy techniques applied to databases and data analysis.
prereq_text: CSC 415 with a C or better, or instructor permission.

title: Artificial Intelligence
description: Search, game playing, intelligent agents, knowledge representation and an introduction to machine learning, with programming assignments.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing or CSC 413 with a C or better, or instructor permission.
notes: Bulletin wording is ambiguous ('upper-division standing or CSC 413'); encoded conservatively as CSC 413.

title: Internet Application Design and Development
description: Full-stack web application development: web protocols, server frameworks, databases, and front-end technologies.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; CSC 413 with a C or better; GPA 3.0 or instructor permission.

title: Deep Learning
description: Neural networks and deep learning: building and training fully connected networks, optimization, and current deep learning trends.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; CSC 510; MATH 225 or MATH 325 with a C or better; GPA 3.0 or instructor permission.

title: Introduction to Database Systems
description: Relational databases and SQL, database design and normalization, query optimization, transactions and concurrency control.
prereq_text: Upper-division standing; CSC 413 with a C or better; GPA 3.0 or instructor permission.

title: Application Development for Mobile Devices
description: Mobile app development with native and cross-platform frameworks, mobile UI design and device APIs.
prereq_text: Senior CS majors; CSC 415 with a C or better; GPA 3.0 or instructor permission.
